assumptions: The complete current individual bearing, axial seat, contact and body loads are fixed; every original signed force and free couple remains. Original self-weight is retained at its source centroid and spread as a local nodal load hypothesis, not a recovered uniform continuum body load.

Only the current four full-width bore-seeded grain-parallel full-front flaws in each cleat are sampled: original radius plus 5 mm on both tips, with each tip separately extended to 10 mm. Unmodeled crack surfaces and other members remain unqualified. No physical drilling or crack is introduced.

The existing unmeasured nine-constant orthotropic material is used in both R/T bindings. Working Ft90=0.2 MPa retains the divisor-two section hypothesis. Common Gc=0.1 N/mm for every mode/mixture is the historical unmeasured hypothesis; Gc=0.05 is an adverse sensitivity. No NDS duration or grade capacity is assigned.

The existing minimum-norm original-side nonseam load mapper uses 15-mm and 30-mm radius increments as separate local boundary hypotheses. Coincident point actions are evaluated on both sides using a 1e-6-mm selection shift with exact counter-couple, preserving their original global wrench. These are not recovered bore/washer pressure fields or compatible bolt-contact laws.
Every intact/initial/final comparison must retain an identical physical prescribed nodal load fingerprint for each boundary hypothesis. No force cloud may silently stitch a crack through seam nodes.

The same source-bound C3D20 staircase geometry is used intact/initial/final. Every actual bore requires positive void sampling, quarter-diameter radial partition bounds and independent local void volume error below 20%; whole retained volume must differ by less than 5% from its own finished BREP. Curved-face stresses are not claimed.

A fully split seam stiffness is assembled once and closed by a proved Boolean congruence for each crack configuration. Right/left reuse requires bit-identical independently generated local nodes and element coordinates. Own case/actions and bore identities remain separate.

Six scalar gauges remove rigid motion only; free and gauge reactions must each satisfy the original 1e-5-N residual gate. Nested fixed-load energies must be nondecreasing. Total free-face G=(Ufinal-Uinitial)/added sound area and contact upper reference=(Ufinal-Uintact)/added area retain all three-dimensional modes.

Peak transverse stress is sampled at 27 Gauss points per intact element; it is neither a continuous maximum nor a converged initiation capacity. The 15/10-mm response comparison is required, with a 20% change guard. A reference exceedance or mesh limit is recorded without redesign.

These finite local comparisons do not bound changes to connected-frame actions when a crack or stiffness changes. Complete cleat, combined joint/member resistance and physical response remain unestablished until their own required proofs are complete. Panel/screw exceedances are deferred, no-slip support remains an assumption, actual observations stay blank.
change_reason: The current 20-mm source-side 15-mm load cloud has only three usable nodes at two base-header contact-point stations. Geometry-only census finds at least four at 15 mm and six at 10 mm. Refine field grids to 15/10 mm; retain the original four-node and full-wrench guards, all current actions and physical geometry.
purpose: Evaluate current three-dimensional mixed-mode finite-bore-flaw energy where a direct mean-stress length construction is unavailable. This is not an external native or revised-frame solve.
